title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page studied sections of the fundamental extension E_{U_S} for an elementary anabelian U over a base. Under the section conjectures, exactly two kinds of sections should occur: (1) sections coming from rational points, which must also be checked to be regular; (2) 'cuspidal' sections coming from K-rational points at infinity. This page asks a global, structural question: to what extent does Conjecture A (or B) of an earlier § allow one to reconstruct, purely group-theoretically, either (i) the category of elementary anabelian varieties over Q, or (ii) the larger category of finitely generated extensions of Q together with elementary anabelian varieties over them? The reconstruction is to be made from the associated exterior Q-groups, or Galois topoi (added in the margin). The only input is the 'fundamental datum': Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q_0), with Q_0 the prime field, acting by outer automorphisms on π̂_{0,3}. Here π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1_Q − {0,1,∞}. This datum gives the extension 1 → π̂_{0,3} → E_{0,3} → Γ_Q → 1.

Step 1, points as sections. Take the sections of E_{0,3} → Γ, counted up to π̂_{0,3}-conjugacy. A sentence was added restricting to 'admissible' sections: those for which the centralizer of (the image of) Γ^0 is trivial. Γ^0 is presumably any open subgroup. Equivalently these are the (admissible) 'points' of the topos B^♮_{π̂_{0,3},Γ}, the classifying topos of the outer action, relative to B^♮_Γ. This gives a set with a Γ-action. The section conjecture predicts that this set is (essentially) U_{0,3}(Q̄), up to the conjecture taken. The admissibility condition looks designed to cut out spurious sections by a group-theoretic condition. Such conditions are standard today: trivial centralizers of open subgroups, 'slimness'.

Step 2, 'drilling holes' (forage des trous). Take a finite Γ-stable set I of such sections, i.e. a finite Γ-stable subset of U_{0,3}(Q̄). One wants to construct group-theoretically an exterior group Π_{0,3}(I) of type (0, 3+card I), carrying a Γ-action. This should be the geometric π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} ∪ I. Iterating this, and passing to the limit over all I, should give (next page) a groupoid version of P^1_Q, the 'arithmetic sphere'. That limit is identified with E_{K_1}, the Galois extension attached to the function field K_1 = Q(T_1). Grothendieck suggests Raynaud-style rigid geometry, with discs around the punctures, to organise the gluing. From there one would climb back up to arbitrary elementary anabelian varieties, i.e. successive fibrations in hyperbolic curves, and to their function fields.

In modern terms, the page sketches a bootstrap programme. Starting only from Γ_Q → Out(π̂_{0,3}), one would recover rational points as sections, then build fundamental groups of curves with more punctures from point-sections (cuspidalization). Going to the limit gives the absolute Galois group of Q(T), and from there all anabelian objects over finitely generated fields.
errors: No outright error. There is a gap: the identification of the set of admissible sections with U_{0,3}(Q̄) depends on the (still open) section conjecture over number fields. The role of the 'trivial centralizer' condition is not justified. The condition is satisfied by genuine point-sections and by cuspidal sections alike, since the cyclotomic character has no invariants on Ẑ(1) for any open subgroup, so it does not by itself distinguish those two kinds of sections.

There is a deeper gap: constructing Π_{0,3}(I) from sections alone is not automatic. One needs extra structure, essentially the outer Galois action on π_1 of configuration spaces (M_{0,4}, M_{0,5}, …) or a cuspidalization theorem. This is exactly the hard step in later work, and the page leaves it as a programme.

ideas.what: Reconstruct the category of elementary anabelian varieties over Q (and over finitely generated fields) group-theoretically from Γ_Q acting outerly on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}).
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian reconstruction / Grothendieck's anabelian programme; outer Galois representation on π̂_{0,3}; I/OM-type statements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); I/OM results by Pop; Ihara, Oda–Matsumoto conjecture
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; Letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (circulated 1981)

ideas.what: Rational points identified with (admissible) conjugacy classes of sections of E_{0,3} → Γ_Q, i.e. points of the topos B^♮_{π̂,Γ} over B^♮_Γ; 'admissible' means trivial centralizer of open subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture; group-theoretic characterisation of geometric sections
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (section conjecture); the topos formulation is in Longue Marche-type notes

ideas.what: 'Forage des trous': from a finite Γ-stable set I of point-sections, construct the exterior group Π_{0,3}(I) of type (0, 3+|I|) with Γ-action.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (Absolute anabelian cuspidalizations, 2007); Hoshi–Mochizuki combinatorial cuspidalization
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche; not in Esquisse explicitly

ideas.what: Limit of hole-drilling gives a groupoid model of P^1_Q (the 'arithmetic sphere'), identified with the Galois extension E_{K_1}, K_1 = Q(T), with Raynaud rigid discs around the punctures (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Absolute Galois group of Q(T) as limit of π_1 of punctured lines; birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pop (birational anabelian), Harbater/Raynaud for rigid patching

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly links the section conjecture (points = sections) to what is now called cuspidalization: constructing π_1 of U minus finitely many points from sections. He uses this as the engine to reconstruct all anabelian varieties and function fields from the single datum Γ_Q ↷ π̂_{0,3}. Mochizuki and Hoshi later developed cuspidalization as a separate theme, without this attribution to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: "forage des trous" doit nous fournir du type (0,3+card I), un groupe extérieur Π_{0,3}(I)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows the cuspidalization problem was conceived by Grothendieck (c. 1981) as a step in a bootstrap from π̂_{0,3} alone. This matters for attribution, and it suggests framing GT/I-OM results as reconstruction from the tripod alone.

missed.claim: The 'admissible section' condition (trivial centralizer of open subgroups) is proposed as a group-theoretic filter on sections of E_{0,3}, phrased as admissible points of the topos B^♮_{π̂,Γ} over B^♮_Γ. It is left unanalysed.
missed.quote: telles que la centralisation de Γ^0 soit triviale (sections "admissibles")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a topos-theoretic formulation of the section set that is not standard in the literature. It is minor, but it relates to the slimness and centralizer results used in combinatorial anabelian geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: The overall anabelian reconstruction programme is known from the Esquisse and the letter to Faltings. The explicit bootstrap starting only from Γ_Q ↷ π̂_{0,3}, via section-points then hole-drilling (cuspidalization) then E_{Q(T)}, is a notable early unpublished articulation. However, it is close to what later work (Mochizuki, Hoshi, Pop) carried out, so it is not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: '[-re-]reconstruire' is just 'reconstruire'; the deleted fragment is a struck-out start of the word.
'(qui n'a ... que[?]' is likely '(qui n'est autre que …', presumably U_{03}(Q̄_0) if the conjecture is admitted.
The last line likely reads 'tout ens. fini I de sections, stable par Γ, la construction' rather than '… fonctions'. It continues on the next page with '« forage des trous »'.
Γ_Q = Γ_{Q̄/Q_0}: Q_0 denotes the prime field Q, not a separate field.
The topos is written B^♮_{π̂_{0,3},Γ_Q} over B^♮_{Γ_Q}; on the page the second one appears as B_{Γ_Q}^♮ (handwritten Γ_Q resembling Γ_6).
